subject: Polity
topic: Directive Principles of State Policy — mixed tiers
description: DPSP: Part IV, classification, key articles, philosophical basis

questions.stem: DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES OF STATE POLICY (DPSP) are in PART ___ of the Constitution.
questions.explanation: DPSP — PART IV, Articles 36-51. NOT JUSTICIABLE (cannot be enforced through courts), but FUNDAMENTAL in governance — state SHOULD be guided by them while making laws. INSPIRED by IRISH Constitution (which got it from Spanish). PURPOSE: lay down economic + social democracy ideals. PHILOSOPHY: GANDHIAN (village panchayats, prohibition, cottage industries), SOCIALIST (welfare state), LIBERAL-INTELLECTUAL (uniform civil code, separation of judiciary, international peace). KEY DPSP: Article 39 (means of livelihood, equal pay for equal work, no exploitation of children), Article 40 (Panchayati Raj), Article 41 (right to work, education), Article 44 (UNIFORM CIVIL CODE — controversial), Article 45 (early childhood education), Article 47 (prohibition of liquor), Article 48 (cow protection!), Article 51 (international peace, dispute settlement).

questions.stem: DPSP source of inspiration in Indian Constitution was the Constitution of:
questions.explanation: DPSP — directly INSPIRED by IRISH Constitution (1937; written by Éamon De Valera, who took it from Spanish 1931 Republic). Irish FRONT NAME: 'Directive Principles of Social Policy'. Indian B.N. Rau (Constitution Adviser) recommended this; Constituent Assembly accepted. INSIGHT — Indian Constitution is a 'BORROWED BAG' but artfully woven: Fundamental Rights (USA), Parliamentary system (UK), Federalism (Canada), Concurrent List (Australia), Emergency provisions (Germany), Citizen Duties (USSR), DPSP (Ireland), etc. AMBEDKAR'S DEFENCE of borrowing: 'There is nothing to be ashamed of in borrowing... I dare say we have only borrowed the basic features... worked out a system suitable for our needs.' India's IS UNIQUE in WEAVING all these together.

options.option_text: Uniform Civil Code (UCC) for all citizens
Free legal aid for poor litigants

questions.explanation: Article 44 (DPSP): 'The state shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a UNIFORM CIVIL CODE throughout the territory of India.' INTENT — common civil law (marriage, divorce, inheritance, adoption) for all religions, replacing personal religious laws (Hindu Marriage Act, Muslim Personal Law, Christian, Parsi, etc.). HIGHLY CONTROVERSIAL — religious + political sensitivities. ONLY GOA has UCC (inherited from Portuguese; called Goa Civil Code). UTTARAKHAND first state to enact UCC in February 2024. SC has called for UCC implementation in multiple judgments (Shah Bano 1985, Sarla Mudgal 1995, John Vallamattom 2003). Other key Article 44 family: Article 39A (free legal aid), 41 (right to work), 43 (living wage), 47 (prohibition + nutrition).

questions.stem: Article 40 (DPSP) directs the state to organise:
questions.explanation: Article 40: state shall take steps to organise VILLAGE PANCHAYATS + endow them with such powers as necessary to function as units of self-government. GANDHIAN VISION — 'Gram Swaraj' (village self-rule). OPERATIONALISED by 73rd Amendment (1992) — added Part IX + 11th Schedule (29 subjects); created mandatory 3-tier panchayati raj (Village, Block, District); reservations for SC/ST + women; Panchayat elections every 5 yrs. Similarly 74th Amendment (1992) — for URBAN local bodies (municipalities, municipal corps). Other GANDHIAN DPSPs: Article 43 (cottage industries), 46 (welfare of SC/ST/weaker sections), 47 (prohibition of intoxicants — operationalised in Bihar, Gujarat, Nagaland), 48 (cow protection), 48A (forest + wildlife). INSIGHT — Gandhi originally wanted Constitution to be more decentralised; partly addressed by these DPSPs + later Panchayati Raj amendments.

questions.stem: When DPSP CONFLICTS with FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, which prevails?
questions.explanation: DPSP vs FR conflict: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS PREVAIL because they're justiciable (FRs enforceable via courts; DPSPs not). KEY CASES: STATE OF MADRAS vs CHAMPAKAM DORAIRAJAN (1951) — court held FR prevails; led to 1st Amendment. CHAMPAKAM CASE: Madras govt's caste-based reservation in college admission (DPSP-aligned, helping backward classes) struck down for violating Article 15 + 29 (FR). 1st Amendment → added Article 15(4) authorising reservation. KESAVANANDA BHARATI (1973) — articulated 'BASIC STRUCTURE'. MINERVA MILLS (1980) → SC struck parts of 42nd Amendment that gave DPSP overriding power (Article 31C). NOW (settled): both FR + DPSP balance — neither absolutely supreme; courts harmonise. RECENT trend: SC reads DPSPs INTO Article 21 (right to life) — environment, education, livelihood, health, food = derived rights.

questions.stem: Which Article of DPSP relates to PROHIBITION OF INTOXICATING DRINKS?
questions.explanation: Article 47: 'Duty of the state to raise the level of NUTRITION + standard of living + IMPROVE PUBLIC HEALTH; specifically, the state shall endeavour to bring about PROHIBITION of intoxicating drinks + drugs which are injurious to health.' GANDHI strongly favoured prohibition. STATES that have implemented (full or partial alcohol prohibition): GUJARAT (since 1960, fully dry), BIHAR (since 2016), NAGALAND, MIZORAM, LAKSHADWEEP. Many other states tried + reversed (Andhra under YSRCP relaxed earlier prohibition; Kerala reversed). PYQ: prohibition is in DPSP → state's CHOICE; not nationwide. ALCOHOL-RELATED state revenue is huge (~25% of state taxes for some states like UP, Maharashtra) — disincentive to prohibition.

options.option_text: NO — non-justiciable but fundamental in governance
Some are; depends on amendment status

questions.explanation: DPSP — NON-JUSTICIABLE (Article 37: 'shall not be enforceable by any court'). BUT 'FUNDAMENTAL in the governance of the country' → state's MORAL OBLIGATION; courts CONSIDER them while interpreting laws + rights. INSIGHT — courts INDIRECTLY enforce DPSPs by reading them into Article 21 (right to life): right to LIVELIHOOD (Olga Tellis, 1985), CLEAN ENVIRONMENT (MC Mehta cases), EDUCATION (Mohini Jain, 1992 — later FR by 86th Amendment), HEALTH, FOOD, SHELTER. AMBEDKAR explanation: DPSPs are 'novel features' of Constitution; while not enforceable now, they should serve as standards courts + governments aspire to. KEY DIFFERENCE: FR are 'Negative obligations' (state shall NOT do X to citizen); DPSP are 'Positive obligations' (state SHALL do Y for citizen).
